title: Square and Triangle
description: Fold a square's four equal sides into 4 x side, add a triangle's three sides, halve a perimeter to work back to a side, and count laps of a side in tenths.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

stage.sizing: the frame is min(100vw, 177.78vh) wide and min(100vh, 56.25vw) tall (dvh where supported); the svg fills it. Nothing scrolls.

bands.header: 0 to 80. One line: the tool name, a measured dot, the phase concept; Hint, sound and restart as round controls far right.
bands.canvas: 92 to 640. One rounded card holding the key at its top right (Answer, Close, Enter, Next, or the Yes / No keys; no question bar), the working area (the whole card until Answer is tapped) and the answer drawer that slides in from the right; the summary page covers it at the end.
bands.footer: 652 to 900. The mascot at the far left on its ground line, the speech bubble beside it (y 656 to 892, the question and every line, printed), one small dot per phase at the right.

zones.layout: board, key only: no question bar, only its key at the right end of the top row (the question is on the bubble); the working area is the whole card (64, 108, 1472 x 520) until the child taps Answer, when the answer drawer (as tall as the working area, the key on its top row reading Close) slides in from the right
zones.controls: circles r 28 at cx 1388, 1460, 1532, cy 40: Hint (data-control again), sound, restart; 72-unit finger boxes
zones.dots: one small dot per phase at the footer's right (72-unit finger boxes, centred on the bubble), no text; in user AND AI mode each is a button (data-control phase-dot, data-phase k) that starts its phase

stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box on the stage. The score leaves on finished and onComplete and is shown once, as stars on the summary page.

writeup.why: Find the perimeter of a square as 4 x side and of a triangle as the sum of its sides, work back to a rectangle's length by halving its perimeter, and find the distance of several laps, with a side in tenths read as tenths.
writeup.look: A square, a triangle or a rectangle on squared paper, a Sum strip under it, a perimeter string on the third phase, and a square path with a lap counter and the Tenths lens on the last.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Square and Triangle' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x 64, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: the number of sides added, or on the last phase the laps walked. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x 64, y 202. The figure lies on squared paper at x 120, y 230 inside a box 560 by 380, drawn to one scale, its given sides labelled deep blue. The Copy side and Times 4 buttons stand at x 760, y 250 and x 760, y 330. The ant walks the boundary, each side lighting vermilion, labelled Boundary, and dropping its length into the Sum strip along y 650 from x 120. On the third phase the perimeter string lies straight at y 600, 820 long, vermilion, and the Halve button at x 760, y 420 folds it; the half lays itself along one length and one breadth of the rectangle, and the Take away tile at x 760, y 500 lifts the breadth off, leaving the length green. On the fourth phase the Tenths lens is a round glass 90 across that shows a side as a count of tenths, and the Lap button and lap counter stand at x 760, y 420. The answer reached is green. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is ten number keys with a point key, a cm key and an m key. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the ten tools of this chapter share them. The lengths the question gives, as a side, a length, a breadth, a height, an edge or a base area, are deep blue, labelled Given or by their own name. The perimeter, area, volume or missing side the working reaches is green, labelled Answer. The boundary that a perimeter walks round is vermilion, labelled Boundary. The unit being counted, one unit square, one unit cube, one row or one layer, is violet, labelled Unit square, Unit cube, Row or Layer. The part squares of an estimate and the space left over where no whole cube fits are rose, labelled More than half, Half or Left over. The side, square, cube, layer or step being worked on now is amber. Grey is kept for a zero holding a place open, and nothing on this stage is ever grey. A square or cube that is not being counted stays warm white inside its near-black outline, grid lines, unit words and signs are near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength. Chrome never borrows one of them, and each reading survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The last figure stays drawn with its boundary vermilion, and the working line under it ends on the answer in green with its unit.

writeup.delight: On the third phase, when the halved string settles along one length and one breadth, the folded half gives a small wave along its whole length and then lies still.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with nothing yet tapped. On the first phase a square lies with one side labelled and three blank, the Copy side button beside it. On the second a triangle lies with its three sides labelled and the ant at a corner. On the third a rectangle lies with its breadth labelled, its length blank, and a vermilion perimeter string laid out beside it. On the fourth a square path lies with the Tenths lens and the Lap button beside it. One thing moves, once: the Copy side button, the ant, the string or the Lap button gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line.
writeup.freePlay: Any square, triangle or rectangle along the grid lines, halved, lapped or read through the Tenths lens. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on squares, triangles, a length worked back from a perimeter, and laps.
voiceLines: A shape on squared paper, ready to walk.
All four sides of a square are equal. How many lots of one side?
Walk all three sides and add them.
Fold the string in half. The half goes along one length and one breadth.
Find one lap first. Then count the laps.
A new shape. Look at its sides first.

observations.why: all four sides of a square are equal.
observations.soWhat: four lots of one side is the perimeter of a square.
observations.observe: Copying one side of the square onto the other three made four equal lengths.

observations.why: a rectangle's boundary is two lengths and two breadths, so half of it is one of each.
observations.soWhat: halve the perimeter first, then take the breadth away to find the length.
observations.observe: The halved string lay exactly along one length and one breadth.

observations.why: every lap of the same path is the same length.
observations.soWhat: find one lap first, then multiply by the number of laps.
observations.observe: Each tap of Lap added the same amount again.

observations.why: each whole metre is ten tenths, and the digit after the point counts tenths.
observations.soWhat: multiply the count of tenths by a whole number, then write the answer back in metres.
observations.observe: Through the lens, a side with a point in it became a whole number of tenths.

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, no colour means good or bad. The miss empties the answer slot at once (every digit, every box, a picked choice), so it is empty through the traceback; the pad re-opens empty after it.
tracebacks: Phase 1: the four sides light one by one, the sum strip reads side + side + side + side, then 4 × side and the perimeter in green
Phase 2: the ant's sides light one by one into the sum strip (a side in metres is lit amber and written in centimetres), ending on the sum in green
Phase 3: the string is halved along one length and one breadth, the breadth is lit amber and taken away, the length lands green and is checked by 2 × (length + breadth)
Phase 4: the lens reads the side in tenths (the word tenths lit amber), the ant walks one lap lighting four sides, then laps × one lap in tenths and the distance in metres in green

voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3, 4: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

question.en: What is the perimeter in cm of a triangle with sides of 1 m, 80 cm and 65 cm?

items.planQuestion: A rectangle has a perimeter of 36 cm and a breadth of 7 cm. How long is it?

question.en: A rectangle has a perimeter of 36 cm and a breadth of 7 cm; how long is it?

items.planQuestion: A rectangle has a perimeter of 20 cm and a breadth of 3 cm. How long is it?

question.en: How long is a rectangle with a perimeter of 20 cm and a breadth of 3 cm?

items.planAnswer: Half of 20 is 10, and 10 - 3 = 7, so the length is 7 cm

items.planQuestion: A rectangle has a perimeter of 50 m and a breadth of 9 m. How long is it?

question.en: A rectangle's perimeter is 50 m and its breadth is 9 m; find its length.

items.planAnswer: Half of 50 is 25, and 25 - 9 = 16, so the length is 16 m

items.planQuestion: A square pond path has sides of 3.4 m. How far is 5 times round it?

question.en: A square pond path has sides of 3.4 m; how far is 5 times round it?

items.planQuestion: One lap round a field is 45 m. How far are 3 laps?

question.en: One lap round a field is 45 m; how far are 3 laps?

items.planQuestion: A square path has sides of 2.6 m. How far is 3 times round it?

question.en: How far do you walk going 3 times round a square path with sides of 2.6 m?

items.planAnswer: 2.6 m is 26 tenths. One lap is 4 x 26 = 104 tenths, which is 10.4 m. Three laps are 3 x 104 = 312 tenths, which is 31.2 m

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once.
